scope: On-foot mouse jumps and repeated NPC animation mesh stalls identified in the 17:33 performance capture.
changes: On-foot yaw/pitch and helicopter mouse dragging use displacement directly, calibrated to previous 60 FPS sensitivity; keyboard/controller input remains a rate.
NPCs prepare idle/walk sections at spawn and reuse bounded cached clips. Cache holds at most 32 poses, except one larger authored clip alone; appearance/species/height changes invalidate it.
All gameplay, forced-animation, baseball, replay and save-restoration frame selection uses the active cached-section offset.
Section visibility only enqueues a render command when it changes. Clip-bind and clip-build CPU trace scopes make future captures attributable.

final_test_summary.validation_note: The full sweep used Multiprocess, which disables config writes in UE. Its sole failing persistence test was rerun with MultiprocessSaveConfig. No game code changed between these runs.

offscreen_benchmark.scope: Controlled D3D12 offscreen animation-transition benchmark including deferred render updates and command flushing; not live-city FPS.

coverage: Same total mouse travel at 30, 60 and 144 FPS plus uneven frames up to 300 ms; yaw/pitch on foot and in helicopter, controller-rate preservation.
Prepared mesh vertex allocations and render proxies survive repeated idle/walk transitions.
Cached geometry matches independent original-builder vertex positions, normals, colors, UVs and indices across human/dog/cow clips, clothing changes and cache eviction.
Only the selected body/head pose is visible; clip and frame identity survive save/restore.

remaining_light_workload.trace_status: High aggregate light-transform time is measured, but the trace does not identify individual lights.
remaining_light_workload.source_review: Vehicle headlights follow moving actors; static street-lamp intensity updates already return when their value is unchanged. This review did not establish an equivalent redundant-update bug.
remaining_light_workload.action: Retained illumination behavior; a fresh attributed capture is needed to isolate the remaining light cost.

limitations: The exact HEVEN2026 mouse-pan route has not been replayed interactively; end-to-end frame pacing still needs a fresh user capture.
The measured ongoing light-transform workload and startup texture-streaming ensures from the earlier investigation are separate remaining issues.
Rare uncached clips may still build geometry; finite cache eviction limits retained memory.

Initial validation hit a sandbox-derived-data-cache denial, then stale UnrealBuildTool source discovery. Both were resolved before the recorded baseline tests. A test fixture compile error was corrected before final builds.
Baseline uses the original mouse and NPC clip-binding paths with the behavior-preserving section-visibility guard already present.
The broad sweep used Multiprocess, which disables config writes in UE ConfigCacheIni.cpp. Its only failing case, SoundVolumePersistence, was rerun with MultiprocessSaveConfig without code changes.
